-- A tokenizer and recursive-descent parser for arithmetic, with variables and errors.

local function tokenize(source)
	local tokens = {}
	local i = 1
	while i <= #source do
		local c = source:sub(i, i)
		if c:match("%s") then
			i += 1
		elseif c:match("%d") then
			local number = source:match("^%d+%.?%d*", i)
			table.insert(tokens, { kind = "number", value = tonumber(number) })
			i += #number
		elseif c:match("[%a_]") then
			local name = source:match("^[%a_][%w_]*", i)
			table.insert(tokens, { kind = "name", value = name })
			i += #name
		elseif c:match("[%+%-%*/%^%(%)=]") then
			table.insert(tokens, { kind = c })
			i += 1
		else
			error(`unexpected character '{c}' at {i}`, 0)
		end
	end
	table.insert(tokens, { kind = "end" })
	return tokens
end

local Parser = {}
Parser.__index = Parser

function Parser.new(tokens, variables)
	return setmetatable({ tokens = tokens, pos = 1, variables = variables }, Parser)
end

function Parser:peek()
	return self.tokens[self.pos].kind
end

function Parser:take(kind)
	local token = self.tokens[self.pos]
	if kind and token.kind ~= kind then
		error(`expected {kind}, got {token.kind}`, 0)
	end
	self.pos += 1
	return token
end

local PRECEDENCE = { ["+"] = 1, ["-"] = 1, ["*"] = 2, ["/"] = 2, ["^"] = 3 }

function Parser:primary()
	local token = self:take()
	if token.kind == "number" then
		return token.value
	elseif token.kind == "name" then
		local value = self.variables[token.value]
		if value == nil then
			error(`unknown variable {token.value}`, 0)
		end
		return value
	elseif token.kind == "-" then
		return -self:expression(3)
	elseif token.kind == "(" then
		local value = self:expression(0)
		self:take(")")
		return value
	end
	error(`unexpected {token.kind}`, 0)
end

function Parser:expression(minimum)
	local left = self:primary()
	while true do
		local op = self:peek()
		local precedence = PRECEDENCE[op]
		if not precedence or precedence <= minimum and op ~= "^" or precedence < minimum then
			return left
		end
		self:take()
		local right = self:expression(op == "^" and precedence - 1 or precedence)
		if op == "+" then
			left += right
		elseif op == "-" then
			left -= right
		elseif op == "*" then
			left *= right
		elseif op == "/" then
			if right == 0 then
				error("division by zero", 0)
			end
			left /= right
		else
			left ^= right
		end
	end
end

local function run(line, variables)
	local tokens = tokenize(line)
	local target
	if tokens[2].kind == "=" then
		target = tokens[1].value
		table.remove(tokens, 1)
		table.remove(tokens, 1)
	end
	local parser = Parser.new(tokens, variables)
	local value = parser:expression(0)
	parser:take("end")
	if target then
		variables[target] = value
	end
	return value
end

local variables = { pi = math.pi }
for _, line in { "x = 2 + 3 * 4", "y = (x - 4) ^ 2 / 2", "x * y - -3", "r = 2", "pi * r ^ 2", "1 / (x - 14)", "z + 1", "3 $ 4" } do
	local ok, result = pcall(run, line, variables)
	print(line, "=>", if ok then string.format("%.4g", result) else `error: {result}`)
end

-- A tokenizer and recursive-descent parser for arithmetic, with variables and errors.

local function tokenize(source)
	local tokens = {}
	local i = 1
	while i <= #source do
		local c = source:sub(i, i)
		if c:match("%s") then
			i += 1
		elseif c:match("%d") then
			local number = source:match("^%d+%.?%d*", i)
			table.insert(tokens, { kind = "number", value = tonumber(number) })
			i += #number
		elseif c:match("[%a_]") then
			local name = source:match("^[%a_][%w_]*", i)
			table.insert(tokens, { kind = "name", value = name })
			i += #name
		elseif c:match("[%+%-%*/%^%(%)=]") then
			table.insert(tokens, { kind = c })
			i += 1

local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local UserInputService = game:GetService("UserInputService")
local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")

local function onCharacter(character)
	local humanoid = character:WaitForChild("Humanoid")
	humanoid.Died:Connect(function()
		print(character.Name, "died")
	end)
end

Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player)
	print("joined", player.Name, player.UserId)
	player.CharacterAdded:Connect(onCharacter)
	player.Chatted:Connect(function(message)
		if message == "/reset" and player.Character then
			player.Character:BreakJoints()
		end
	end)
end)

workspace.ChildAdded:Connect(function(child)
	if child:IsA("BasePart") then
		child.Anchored = true
	end
end)

local pad = workspace:WaitForChild("Pad")
pad.Touched:Connect(function(hit)
	local owner = Players:GetPlayerFromCharacter(hit.Parent)
	if owner then
		print(owner.Name, "touched the pad")
	end
end)

UserInputService.InputBegan:Connect(function(input, gameProcessed)
	if not gameProcessed and input.KeyCode == Enum.KeyCode.E then
		print("interact")
	end
end)

local elapsed = 0
RunService.Heartbeat:Connect(function(deltaTime)
	elapsed += deltaTime
end)

for _, child in ipairs(workspace:GetChildren()) do
	print(child.Name)
end

for _, descendant in workspace:GetDescendants() do
	if descendant:IsA("Light") then
		descendant.Enabled = false
	end
end

for _, player in pairs(Players:GetPlayers()) do
	print(player.DisplayName, elapsed)
end

	print("pairs", i, v)

-- returning a closure or next, objects with __call, coroutines, and pairs and ipairs, which the
-- compiler turns into their own loop instructions
local function keys(t)
	local out = {}
	for k in t do
		table.insert(out, tostring(k))
	end
	table.sort(out)
	return table.concat(out, ",")
end

local list = { "a", "b", "c" }
for i, v in list do
	print("plain", i, v)
end
for i, v in ipairs(list) do
	print("ipairs", i, v)
end
for i, v in pairs(list) do
	print("pairs", i, v)
end
print(keys({ x = 1, y = 2, [3] = true, [true] = 0 }))

-- a hole: ipairs stops at it, a plain loop and pairs walk past it
local holes = { 1, 2, nil, 4 }
local viaIpairs, viaPlain, viaPairs = 0, 0, 0
for _ in ipairs(holes) do
	viaIpairs += 1
end
for _ in holes do
	viaPlain += 1
end
for _ in pairs(holes) do
	viaPairs += 1
end
print(viaIpairs, viaPlain, viaPairs)

-- __iter returning a stateful closure
local Range = {}
Range.__index = Range
Range.__iter = function(self)
	local i = self.from - self.step
	return function()
		i += self.step
		if i <= self.to then
			return i, i * i
		end
		return nil
	end
end
local function range(from, to, step)
	return setmetatable({ from = from, to = to, step = step or 1 }, Range)
end
for v, sq in range(1, 7, 3) do
	print("range", v, sq)
end

-- __iter handing back next and another table to walk
local Bag = {
	__iter = function(self)
		return next, self.items
	end,
}
local bag = setmetatable({ items = { "x", "y" }, hidden = true }, Bag)
for k, v in bag do
	print("bag", k, v)
end

-- an object with __call is the iterator function itself
local countdown = setmetatable({ n = 3 }, {
	__call = function(self)
		if self.n > 0 then
			self.n -= 1
			return self.n + 1
		end
		return nil
	end,
})
for v in countdown do
	print("countdown", v)
end

-- a coroutine as the iterator
for v in coroutine.wrap(function()
	for i = 1, 3 do
		coroutine.yield(i * 2)
	end
end) do
	print("co", v)
end

-- continue, break and writing the loop variable inside generalized loops
for i, v in list do
	if v == "b" then
		continue
	end
	i *= 10
	print("skip b", i, v)
end
local found
for i, v in { 5, 6, 7, 8 } do
	if v % 2 == 1 and i > 1 then
		found = i
		break
	end
end
print("found", found)

-- nested loops over the same table, the inner one reading the outer's variables
local grid = { { 1, 2 }, { 3, 4 } }
local sum = 0
for r, row in grid do
	for c, cell in row do
		sum += cell * r * c
	end
end
print("grid", sum)

-- a table changed between loops is walked as it is now
local growing = { 1 }
for round = 1, 3 do
	local seen = 0
	for _ in growing do
		seen += 1
	end
	growing[#growing + 1] = round
	print("round", round, seen)
end

-- Luau's experimental `if local` / `while local` / `const` syntax (a friend's case). The binding
-- lives only in the then-branch or loop body, so an outer variable with the same name has to
-- stay visible in the else-branch, and every loop iteration gets a fresh local for closures.
do
	const t = {1, 2, 3}
	while local v = table.remove(t) do
		print(v, #t)
	end
end
do
	local items = {"a", "b", false, "c"}
	local i = 0
	local function nextItem()
		i += 1
		return items[i]
	end
	-- false ends the loop just like nil
	while const item = nextItem() do
		print("item", item)
	end
	print("stopped at", i)
end
do
	local fns = {}
	local queue = {10, 20, 30}
	while local n = table.remove(queue, 1) do
		table.insert(fns, function()
			return n
		end)
	end
	print(fns[1](), fns[2](), fns[3]())
end
do
	local x = "outer"
	if local x = nil then
		print("then", x)
	else
		print("else", x)
	end
	if local x = "inner" then
		print("then", x)
	end
	print("after", x)
end
do
	local function classify(s)
		if local n: number? = tonumber(s) then
			return "number " .. n * 2
		elseif local first = string.match(s, "^%a+") then
			return "word " .. first
		elseif const sym = string.match(s, "^%p") then
			return "symbol " .. sym
		else
			return "other"
		end
	end
	print(classify("21"), classify("hello world"), classify("!?"), classify("  "))
end
do
	local function lookup(t, k)
		return if local v = t[k] then v .. "!" else "missing"
	end
	local map = {a = "x", b = "y"}
	print(lookup(map, "a"), lookup(map, "z"))
	const limit = 3
	local count = 0
	while local v = count < limit and count do
		count = v + 1
	end
	print("count", count)
end

-- Luau's experimental `if local` / `while local` / `const` syntax (a friend's case). The binding
-- lives only in the then-branch or loop body, so an outer variable with the same name has to
-- stay visible in the else-branch, and every loop iteration gets a fresh local for closures.
do
	const t = {1, 2, 3}
	while local v = table.remove(t) do
		print(v, #t)
	end
end
do
	local items = {"a", "b", false, "c"}
	local i = 0
	local function nextItem()
		i += 1
		return items[i]
	end
	-- false ends the loop just like nil
	while const item = nextItem() do
		print("item", item)
	end
	print("stopped at", i)
end
do
	local fns = {}
	local queue = {10, 20, 30}
	while local n = table.remove(queue, 1) do
		table.insert(fns, function()
			return n
		end)
	end
	print(fns[1](), fns[2](), fns[3]())
end
do
	local x = "outer"
	if local x = nil then
		print("then", x)
	else
		print("else", x)
	end
	if local x = "inner" then
		print("then", x)
	end
	print("after", x)
end
do
	local function classify(s)
		if local n: number? = tonumber(s) then
			return "number " .. n * 2
		elseif local first = string.match(s, "^%a+") then
			return "word " .. first
		elseif const sym = string.match(s, "^%p") then
			return "symbol " .. sym
		else
			return "other"
		end
	end
	print(classify("21"), classify("hello world"), classify("!?"), classify("  "))
end
do
	local function lookup(t, k)
		return if local v = t[k] then v .. "!" else "missing"
	end
	local map = {a = "x", b = "y"}
	print(lookup(map, "a"), lookup(map, "z"))
	const limit = 3
	local count = 0
	while local v = count < limit and count do
		count = v + 1
	end
	print("count", count)
end

--!strict
-- An inventory with stacking, weight limits and a sorted report.

local Inventory = {}
Inventory.__index = Inventory

local ITEMS = {
	sword = { weight = 8, stack = 1, value = 120 },
	potion = { weight = 1, stack = 10, value = 25 },
	arrow = { weight = 0.1, stack = 64, value = 1 },
	shield = { weight = 12, stack = 1, value = 90 },
}

function Inventory.new(capacity)
	local self = setmetatable({}, Inventory)
	self.capacity = capacity
	self.slots = {}
	self.weight = 0
	return self
end

local function round(n, places)
	local scale = 10 ^ places
	return math.floor(n * scale + 0.5) / scale
end

function Inventory:add(name, count)
	local info = ITEMS[name]
	if not info then
		return false, `unknown item {name}`
	end
	if self.weight + info.weight * count > self.capacity then
		return false, `too heavy: {round(self.weight + info.weight * count, 1)} > {self.capacity}`
	end
	local left = count
	for _, slot in self.slots do
		if slot.name == name and slot.count < info.stack then
			local moved = math.min(info.stack - slot.count, left)
			slot.count += moved
			left -= moved
			if left == 0 then
				break
			end
		end
	end
	while left > 0 do
		local moved = math.min(info.stack, left)
		table.insert(self.slots, { name = name, count = moved })
		left -= moved
	end
	self.weight += info.weight * count
	return true
end

function Inventory:remove(name, count)
	for i = #self.slots, 1, -1 do
		local slot = self.slots[i]
		if slot.name ~= name then
			continue
		end
		local taken = math.min(slot.count, count)
		slot.count -= taken
		count -= taken
		self.weight -= ITEMS[name].weight * taken
		if slot.count == 0 then
			table.remove(self.slots, i)
		end
		if count == 0 then
			return true
		end
	end
	return count == 0
end

function Inventory:report()
	local totals = {}
	for _, slot in self.slots do
		totals[slot.name] = (totals[slot.name] or 0) + slot.count
	end
	local names = {}
	for name in totals do
		table.insert(names, name)
	end
	table.sort(names, function(a, b)
		return ITEMS[a].value * totals[a] > ITEMS[b].value * totals[b]
	end)
	local lines = {}
	for rank, name in names do
		lines[rank] = `{rank}. {name} x{totals[name]} ({ITEMS[name].value * totals[name]}g)`
	end
	return table.concat(lines, "\n"), round(self.weight, 2)
end

local bag = Inventory.new(40)
print(bag:add("arrow", 150))
print(bag:add("potion", 12))
print(bag:add("sword", 1))
print(bag:add("shield", 3))
print(bag:add("wand", 1))
print(bag:remove("arrow", 70), bag:remove("potion", 20))
print(bag:report())

-- metamethods: arithmetic, comparison, concat, call, index and newindex functions, len and unm,
-- and the raw functions that skip them
local Vec = {}
Vec.__index = Vec
local function vec(x, y)
	return setmetatable({ x = x, y = y }, Vec)
end
Vec.__add = function(a, b)
	return vec(a.x + b.x, a.y + b.y)
end
Vec.__sub = function(a, b)
	return vec(a.x - b.x, a.y - b.y)
end
Vec.__mul = function(a, b)
	if type(a) == "number" then
		return vec(a * b.x, a * b.y)
	end
	return vec(a.x * b, a.y * b)
end
Vec.__unm = function(a)
	return vec(-a.x, -a.y)
end
Vec.__eq = function(a, b)
	return a.x == b.x and a.y == b.y
end
Vec.__lt = function(a, b)
	return a.x * a.x + a.y * a.y < b.x * b.x + b.y * b.y
end
Vec.__le = function(a, b)
	return not (b < a)
end
Vec.__len = function(a)
	return math.sqrt(a.x * a.x + a.y * a.y)
end
Vec.__concat = function(a, b)
	local function s(v)
		return if type(v) == "table" then `({v.x}, {v.y})` else tostring(v)
	end
	return s(a) .. s(b)
end
Vec.__call = function(self, k)
	return self[k]
end
function Vec:dot(o)
	return self.x * o.x + self.y * o.y
end

-- multiple assignment and multiple returns: every right-hand side is read before anything is
-- assigned, a call in the middle of a list is cut to one value, and parentheses cut it too
local function three()
	return 1, 2, 3
end
local function none() end

local a, b, c = 1, 2, 3
a, b, c = c, a, b
print(a, b, c)

local t = { 10, 20, 30 }
local i = 1
i, t[i] = i + 1, "x" -- the index is read before i changes
print(i, t[1], t[2])

local x, y, z = three(), 10
print(x, y, z)
print((three()))
print(three(), three())
print(#{ three(), three() }, #{ (three()), three() }, select("#", none()), select("#", (none())))

local function count(...)
	return select("#", ...)
end
print(count(nil, nil), count(none()), count(none(), nil), count(three()))

local function tail(...)
	local first, rest = ..., select(2, ...)
	return first, rest, select(-1, ...)
end
print(tail(4, 5, 6))

-- a swap through a table and a local in one statement
local cell = { v = 1 }
local held = 2
cell.v, held = held, cell.v
print(cell.v, held)

-- varargs captured into a table with holes
local function pack(...)
	return { n = select("#", ...), ... }
end
local p = pack(1, nil, 3, nil)
print(p.n, p[1], p[2], p[3], p[4])

-- assignment to a local that a later expression in the same list reads
local m = 1
local n
m, n = m + 1, m
print(m, n)

-- compound assignment whose index expression has a side effect, evaluated once
local calls = 0
local function idx()
	calls += 1
	return 2
end
local arr = { 1, 2, 3 }
arr[idx()] += 10
arr[idx()] ..= ""
print(arr[2], calls)

-- comparisons a decompiler can't flip: with NaN, `not (a < b)` isn't `a >= b`, and `x ~= x` is
-- true. Also and/or chains where a false or nil value in the middle changes which side wins
local nan = 0 / 0
local values = { 1, -1, 0, nan, math.huge, -math.huge }

local function compare(a, b)
	local out = {}
	if not (a < b) then out[#out + 1] = "!lt" end
	if not (a <= b) then out[#out + 1] = "!le" end
	if not (a > b) then out[#out + 1] = "!gt" end
	if not (a >= b) then out[#out + 1] = "!ge" end
	if a ~= a then out[#out + 1] = "self" end
	if not (a == b) then out[#out + 1] = "!eq" end
	while not (a < b) do
		out[#out + 1] = "w"
		break
	end
	local rounds = 0
	repeat
		rounds += 1
		out[#out + 1] = "r"
	until not (a > b) or rounds == 2
	return table.concat(out, ",")
end

for i = 1, #values do
	for j = 1, #values do
		print(i, j, compare(values[i], values[j]))
	end
end

-- values, not just truthiness
local function pick(a, b, c)
	local x = a and b or c
	local y = a and (b or c)
	local z = (a or b) and c
	local w = not a == not b
	local v = a and false or c
	local u = a == nil and b or nil
	return x, y, z, w, v, u
end
local samples = { true, false, nil, 0, "", nan }
for i = 1, 6 do
	for j = 1, 6 do
		for k = 1, 6 do
			local a, b, c = samples[i], samples[j], samples[k]
			print(i, j, k, pick(a, b, c))
		end
	end
end

-- a guard whose branches both fall through, around a comparison with a constant on the left
local count = 0
for _, v in ipairs(values) do
	if 0 < v then
		count += 1
	elseif not (0 >= v) then
		count += 100
	end
end
print("count", count)

-- metatable classes with methods
local Account = {}
Account.__index = Account

function Account.new(owner, balance)
	local self = setmetatable({}, Account)
	self.owner = owner
	self.balance = balance or 0
	self.history = {}
	return self
end

function Account:deposit(amount)
	if amount <= 0 then
		error("deposit must be positive")
	end
	self.balance += amount
	table.insert(self.history, { kind = "deposit", amount = amount })
end

function Account:withdraw(amount)
	if amount > self.balance then
		return false, "insufficient funds"
	end
	self.balance -= amount
	table.insert(self.history, { kind = "withdraw", amount = amount })
	return true
end

function Account:statement()
	local lines = {}
	for index, entry in ipairs(self.history) do
		lines[index] = ("%s %d"):format(entry.kind, entry.amount)
	end
	return table.concat(lines, "\n")
end

local savings = Account.new("sam", 100)
savings:deposit(50)
local ok, reason = savings:withdraw(500)
if not ok then
	print(reason)
end
print(savings:statement())

-- A* on a small grid map, with a binary heap for the open set.

local MAP = {
	"S....#....",
	".##..#.##.",
	".#...#..#.",
	".#.###..#.",
	"...#....#G",
	"##.#.####.",
	"..........",
}

local function parse(rows)
	local grid, start, goal = {}, nil, nil
	for y, row in ipairs(rows) do
		grid[y] = {}
		for x = 1, #row do
			local c = row:sub(x, x)
			grid[y][x] = c ~= "#"
			if c == "S" then
				start = { x = x, y = y }
			elseif c == "G" then
				goal = { x = x, y = y }
			end
		end
	end
	return grid, start, goal
end

local function key(x, y)
	return y * 1000 + x
end

local function heuristic(a, b)
	return math.abs(a.x - b.x) + math.abs(a.y - b.y)
end

local Heap = {}
Heap.__index = Heap

function Heap.new()
	return setmetatable({ items = {}, size = 0 }, Heap)
end

function Heap:push(node, priority)
	self.size += 1
	local i = self.size
	self.items[i] = { node = node, priority = priority }
	while i > 1 do
		local parent = i // 2
		if self.items[parent].priority <= self.items[i].priority then
			break
		end
		self.items[parent], self.items[i] = self.items[i], self.items[parent]
		i = parent
	end
end

function Heap:pop()
	if self.size == 0 then
		return nil
	end
	local top = self.items[1]
	self.items[1] = self.items[self.size]
	self.items[self.size] = nil
	self.size -= 1
	local i = 1
	while true do
		local smallest, left, right = i, i * 2, i * 2 + 1
		if left <= self.size and self.items[left].priority < self.items[smallest].priority then
			smallest = left
		end
		if right <= self.size and self.items[right].priority < self.items[smallest].priority then
			smallest = right
		end
		if smallest == i then
			break
		end
		self.items[smallest], self.items[i] = self.items[i], self.items[smallest]
		i = smallest
	end
	return top.node
end

local DIRECTIONS = { { 1, 0 }, { -1, 0 }, { 0, 1 }, { 0, -1 } }

local function findPath(grid, start, goal)
	local open = Heap.new()
	local cameFrom, cost = {}, { [key(start.x, start.y)] = 0 }
	open:push(start, heuristic(start, goal))
	local visited = 0
	while open.size > 0 do
		local current = open:pop()
		visited += 1
		if current.x == goal.x and current.y == goal.y then
			local path = { current }
			local k = key(current.x, current.y)
			while cameFrom[k] do
				current = cameFrom[k]
				table.insert(path, 1, current)
				k = key(current.x, current.y)
			end
			return path, visited
		end
		for _, d in DIRECTIONS do
			local nx, ny = current.x + d[1], current.y + d[2]
			if not (grid[ny] and grid[ny][nx]) then
				continue
			end
			local nk = key(nx, ny)
			local newCost = cost[key(current.x, current.y)] + 1
			if cost[nk] == nil or newCost < cost[nk] then
				cost[nk] = newCost
				cameFrom[nk] = current
				local next = { x = nx, y = ny }
				open:push(next, newCost + heuristic(next, goal))
			end
		end
	end
	return nil, visited
end

local grid, start, goal = parse(MAP)
local path, visited = findPath(grid, start, goal)
if path then
	local steps = {}
	for i, p in path do
		steps[i] = `({p.x},{p.y})`
	end
	print(`found a path of {#path - 1} steps after visiting {visited} cells`)

end

local MAP = {
	"S....#....",
	".##..#.##.",
	".#...#..#.",
	".#.###..#.",
	"...#....#G",
	"##.#.####.",
	"..........",
}

local function parse(rows)
	local grid, start, goal = {}, nil, nil
	for y, row in ipairs(rows) do
		grid[y] = {}
		for x = 1, #row do
			local c = row:sub(x, x)
			grid[y][x] = c ~= "#"
			if c == "S" then
				start = { x = x, y = y }
			elseif c == "G" then
				goal = { x = x, y = y }
			end
		end
	end
	return grid, start, goal
end

local function key(x, y)
	return y * 1000 + x
end

local function heuristic(a, b)
	return math.abs(a.x - b.x) + math.abs(a.y - b.y)
end

local Heap = {}
Heap.__index = Heap

function Heap.new()
	return setmetatable({ items = {}, size = 0 }, Heap)
end

function Heap:push(node, priority)
	self.size += 1
	local i = self.size
	self.items[i] = { node = node, priority = priority }
	while i > 1 do
		local parent = i // 2
		if self.items[parent].priority <= self.items[i].priority then
			break
		end
		self.items[parent], self.items[i] = self.items[i], self.items[parent]
		i = parent
	end
end

function Heap:pop()
	if self.size == 0 then
		return nil
	end
	local top = self.items[1]
	self.items[1] = self.items[self.size]
	self.items[self.size] = nil
	self.size -= 1
	local i = 1

		local smallest, left, right = i, i * 2, i * 2 + 1
		if left <= self.size and self.items[left].priority < self.items[smallest].priority then
			smallest = left
		end
		if right <= self.size and self.items[right].priority < self.items[smallest].priority then
			smallest = right
		end
		if smallest == i then
			break
		end
		self.items[smallest], self.items[i] = self.items[i], self.items[smallest]
		i = smallest
	end
	return top.node
end

local function findPath(grid, start, goal)
	local open = Heap.new()

--!rosetta-options +t1
-- type syntax, which compiles to nothing, compiled with type information on (+t1): every
-- function carries its parameter types in the bytecode, which a decompiler has to read past,
-- and casts, generics, packs and attributes all have to come back as valid Luau
type Vec = { x: number, y: number }
export type Shape = { kind: "circle", r: number } | { kind: "rect", w: number, h: number }
type Callback<T> = (T, ...any) -> boolean
type Pair<K, V> = { key: K, value: V }

local function add(a: Vec, b: Vec): Vec
	return { x = a.x + b.x, y = a.y + b.y }
end

local function area(s: Shape): number
	if s.kind == "circle" then
		return math.floor(3 * s.r * s.r)
	end
	return (s :: any).w * (s :: any).h
end

local function first<T>(list: { T }, pred: Callback<T>): T?
	for _, v in list do
		if pred(v) then
			return v
		end
	end
	return nil
end

local function count(...: number): (number, number)
	local total = 0
	for i = 1, select("#", ...) do
		total += (select(i, ...))
	end
	return select("#", ...), total
end

local v = add({ x = 1, y = 2 }, { x = 3, y = 4 })
print(v.x, v.y)
print(area({ kind = "circle", r = 2 }), area({ kind = "rect", w = 3, h = 4 }))
print(first({ 1, 5, 8 }, function(n: number): boolean
	return n > 4
end))
print(count(1, 2, 3))

-- every primitive the type information can name, as parameters and typed locals
local function describe(n: number, s: string, t: { any }, f: () -> (), b: buffer, flag: boolean?, vec: vector, th: thread): string
	local size: number = buffer.len(b)
	local parts: { string } = { tostring(n), s, tostring(#t), type(f), tostring(size), tostring(flag), tostring(vec.y), type(th) }
	return table.concat(parts, " ")
end
local y = v.x // 2
print(describe(1.5, "s", { 1, 2 }, function() end, buffer.create(4), nil, vector.create(1, y, 3), coroutine.create(print)))

local function many(): ...number
	return 1, 2, 3
end
print((many() :: number), many())
local text = ("x" :: string):rep(3)
print(text, (#text :: number) + 1)

-- methods with an annotated self, and a type taken from a value
type Account = { balance: number, deposit: (Account, number) -> Account }
local Account = {}
Account.__index = Account
function Account.new(balance: number): Account
	return setmetatable({ balance = balance }, Account) :: any
end
function Account.deposit(self: Account, amount: number): Account
	self.balance += amount

end
local acct = Account.new(10)
type AccountValue = typeof(acct)
local same: AccountValue = acct:deposit(5):deposit(2.5)

local scale = @native function(x: number, k: number): number

	return a + (b - a) * t

type Vec = { x: number, y: number }
export type Shape = { kind: "circle", r: number } | { kind: "rect", w: number, h: number }
type Callback<T> = (T, ...any) -> boolean
type Pair<K, V> = { key: K, value: V }

local function add(a: Vec, b: Vec): Vec
	return { x = a.x + b.x, y = a.y + b.y }
end

local function area(s: Shape): number
	if s.kind == "circle" then
		return math.floor(3 * s.r * s.r)
	end
	return (s :: any).w * (s :: any).h
end

local function first<T>(list: { T }, pred: Callback<T>): T?
	for _, v in list do
		if pred(v) then
			return v
		end
	end
	return nil
end

local function count(...: number): (number, number)
	local total = 0
	for i = 1, select("#", ...) do
		total += (select(i, ...))
	end
	return select("#", ...), total
end

local v = add({ x = 1, y = 2 }, { x = 3, y = 4 })
print(v.x, v.y)
print(area({ kind = "circle", r = 2 }), area({ kind = "rect", w = 3, h = 4 }))
print(first({ 1, 5, 8 }, function(n: number): boolean
	return n > 4
end))
print(count(1, 2, 3))

-- every primitive the type information can name, as parameters and typed locals
local function describe(n: number, s: string, t: { any }, f: () -> (), b: buffer, flag: boolean?, vec: vector, th: thread): string
	local size: number = buffer.len(b)
	local parts: { string } = { tostring(n), s, tostring(#t), type(f), tostring(size), tostring(flag), tostring(vec.y), type(th) }
	return table.concat(parts, " ")
end

	return 1, 2, 3
end

-- vectors: vector.create with constant arguments folds into a vector constant, which has to come
-- back as something vanilla Luau runs (Roblox spells it Vector3.new, plain Luau doesn't have
-- that), plus vector arithmetic, components and the vector library, which compile to fast calls
local function show(v)
	return string.format("%g,%g,%g", v.x, v.y, v.z)
end

local up = vector.create(0, 1, 0)
local unit = vector.create(1, 1, 1)
print(show(up), show(unit), typeof(up), up == vector.create(0, 1, 0))
print(show(vector.create(-0, 0.5, 1e300)), show(vector.create(1 / 3, 2 ^ 20, -7)))

-- arithmetic with vectors and numbers, and unary minus
local a, b = vector.create(1, 2, 3), vector.create(4, 5, 6)
print(show(a + b), show(a - b), show(a * b), show(b / a), show(a * 2), show(3 / b), show(-a), show(b // a))

-- components, and arguments known only at run time
local n = #"abcd"
local v = vector.create(n, n * 2, n // 3)
print(v.x, v.y, v.z, v.X, v.Y, v.Z)

-- the vector library
print(vector.magnitude(vector.create(3, 4, 0)), show(vector.normalize(vector.create(0, 0, 9))))
print(vector.dot(a, b), show(vector.cross(a, b)), show(vector.floor(vector.create(1.5, -1.5, 2))))
print(show(vector.ceil(vector.create(1.2, -1.2, 0))), show(vector.abs(vector.create(-1, 2, -3))))
print(show(vector.sign(vector.create(-5, 0, 5))), show(vector.clamp(vector.create(5, -5, 0), vector.zero, vector.one)))
print(show(vector.max(a, b, vector.create(9, 0, 0))), show(vector.min(a, b)), vector.angle(vector.create(1, 0, 0), up))
print(show(vector.zero), show(vector.one))

-- vectors as table keys and in comparisons
local seen = {}
seen[vector.create(1, 2, 3)] = "found"

-- vectors: vector.create with constant arguments folds into a vector constant, which has to come
-- back as something vanilla Luau runs (Roblox spells it Vector3.new, plain Luau doesn't have
-- that), plus vector arithmetic, components and the vector library, which compile to fast calls
local function show(v)
	return string.format("%g,%g,%g", v.x, v.y, v.z)
end

local up = vector.create(0, 1, 0)
local unit = vector.create(1, 1, 1)
print(show(up), show(unit), typeof(up), up == vector.create(0, 1, 0))
print(show(vector.create(-0, 0.5, 1e300)), show(vector.create(1 / 3, 2 ^ 20, -7)))

-- arithmetic with vectors and numbers, and unary minus
local a, b = vector.create(1, 2, 3), vector.create(4, 5, 6)
print(show(a + b), show(a - b), show(a * b), show(b / a), show(a * 2), show(3 / b), show(-a), show(b // a))

-- components, and arguments known only at run time
local n = #"abcd"
local v = vector.create(n, n * 2, n // 3)
print(v.x, v.y, v.z, v.X, v.Y, v.Z)

-- the vector library
print(vector.magnitude(vector.create(3, 4, 0)), show(vector.normalize(vector.create(0, 0, 9))))
print(vector.dot(a, b), show(vector.cross(a, b)), show(vector.floor(vector.create(1.5, -1.5, 2))))
print(show(vector.ceil(vector.create(1.2, -1.2, 0))), show(vector.abs(vector.create(-1, 2, -3))))
print(show(vector.sign(vector.create(-5, 0, 5))), show(vector.clamp(vector.create(5, -5, 0), vector.zero, vector.one)))
print(show(vector.max(a, b, vector.create(9, 0, 0))), show(vector.min(a, b)), vector.angle(vector.create(1, 0, 0), up))
print(show(vector.zero), show(vector.one))

-- vectors as table keys and in comparisons
local seen = {}
seen[vector.create(1, 2, 3)] = "found"
print(seen[a], a == vector.create(1, 2, 3), a ~= b)
